items.notes: Quote: "When TType is an object and TWith is `unknown` (or `any`), the new Overwrite returns `unknown`/`any` and drops TType... Any caller that passes a TWith of `unknown`... (a middleware `_ctx_out`...) now erases the accumulated ctx or input type." This is GT-j3's mechanism: the non-object TWith branch replaces an object context at the ctx merge. Scratch tsc probe (clone-work/probe-{base,head}.ts, clone's tsc 5.x, --strict): an unknown ctx override gives TS2339 on ctx.base at head only, and the `X|undefined` override gives TS18048 at head only. The item's passing mention of `Overwrite<any,{b:2}>` junk touches GT-j2 without the consequence; the primary claim is the GT-j3 one. No fix is proposed, so absent.

Quote: "The `object` check still treats arrays and functions as objects, so `Overwrite<string[], {b:2}>` is key-merged... The fix is only partial." Array and function operands also took the key-wise mapped branch at the merge-base; the mapped body did not change. Scratch tsc probe (clone-work/probe-{base,head}.ts, clone's tsc 5.x, --strict): Eq<Overwrite<string[],string[]>, string[]> is false at both base and head. So this is an accurate observation of a pre-existing limitation, not a defect introduced by the PR.

Quote: "`Overwrite<{a:1}|undefined, {b:2}|undefined>` gives `{b:2} | {a:1;b:2} | undefined`. The `{b:2}` member drops `a`... infers an input type that no longer requires `a`." The old Overwrite distributed over both parameters too, and produced the `{b:2}` member (plus `{a:1}` and `{}`). Scratch tsc probe (clone-work/probe-{base,head}.ts, clone's tsc 5.x, --strict): assigning `{b:2}` to that Overwrite compiles at both base and head. For `.input(optional obj).use(next)` the head is stricter than base (base accepted `{}`, head rejects it). The asserted input regression is not introduced by the PR, and the middleware-input `{b}|undefined` scenario is not substantiated.

Quote: "`Overwrite<string, never>` and `Overwrite<{a:1}, never>` both evaluate to `never`, not TType. The `: TType` branch is dead code." True, but it is only a doc and dead-code point. Overwrite<X, never> is never at the merge-base too (the old `TType extends any ? TWith extends any` also distributed over never; my probe's Eq<Overwrite<{a:1},never>, never> holds at both commits), so nothing regresses. The register's non_defects cover the `TWith extends any` / factoring remarks. Below the finding threshold.
Quote: "The conditional is needlessly nested. `X extends any ? Y : never` is a no-op wrapper". A factoring preference; the register's non_defects rule it not a defect.

Quote: "The fix is made in the shared `Overwrite` helper, which also computes `_ctx_out` and middleware ctx, instead of at the input-merging site... wide blast radius." This is a design and placement critique. The facts are accurate: Overwrite is used at the ctx sites, and OverwriteIfDefined exists at procedureBuilder.ts:69. It names no concrete defect beyond deferring to item 1, so it is an observation below the threshold.

Quote: "The regression test is thin... it never asserts the `voidWithMiddleware` procedure it defines." A test-coverage and hygiene remark; the register lists the voidWithMiddleware gap as a non-defect.
Quote: "The test file is named `issue-5020` but the PR is #5017." Accurate traceability and naming hygiene, below the threshold.

Quote: "With `initTRPC.context<any>().create()` and `t.procedure.use(o => o.next({ ctx: { x: 1 } })).query(({ ctx }) => ctx.foo.bar)`, tsc on review-head reports TS2339... The same code compiled cleanly on main". This is GT-j2's trigger, mechanism (`any extends object` resolves to both branches) and consequence exactly, matching the register's reproduction. No fix is proposed (Fix: —), so absent.

Quote: "A non-object TWith (unknown, any, undefined, string) now replaces an object TType wholesale... Overwrite<{a:1}, undefined> gives `undefined`... Any place where `_ctx_out` is or becomes `unknown` or `undefined` now wipes out the previously accumulated ctx". This is GT-j3's mechanism, and it names the undefined override at the ctx call sites (middleware.ts:65/81/103, procedureBuilder.ts:38, ResolveOptions). Scratch tsc probe (clone-work/probe-{base,head}.ts, clone's tsc 5.x, --strict): `next({ ctx: maybe })` with `{extra}|undefined` gives TS18048 at head only. No fix is proposed, so absent.

Quote: "Leftover twoslash `// ^?` debugging markers, an unnecessary `async`... The eight-commit history was merged unsquashed". Hygiene and style.

Quote: "The nested conditionals are more complex than needed... the mapped type still drops optional modifiers". The factoring point is a register non-defect. The optional-modifier loss is pre-existing, because the mapped body is unchanged by the PR.

Quote: "Overwrite still merges any two object-like types key by key. Arrays and functions extend `object`, so array inputs come out mangled". Array and function operands also took the key-wise mapped branch at the merge-base; the mapped body did not change. Scratch tsc probe (clone-work/probe-{base,head}.ts, clone's tsc 5.x, --strict): Eq<Overwrite<string[],string[]>, string[]> is false at both base and head. So this is an accurate observation of a pre-existing limitation, not a defect introduced by the PR. `Overwrite<{a:1}, () => void>` yields {a:1} at base as well. The chained-`.input()` example is also off, since `.input()` merges through OverwriteIfDefined (procedureBuilder.ts:69), not Overwrite.

Quote: "`Overwrite<any, {a:1}>` evaluates to `{a:1} | { [x: string]: any; ... }`, because `any extends object` takes both branches. If the ctx or input type is `any`, that index-signature branch leaks into the inferred type." This names GT-j2's mechanism and trigger (an any ctx overwritten by a middleware). The consequence is only 'garbage union' / 'leaks', not the TS2339, but it leads a reader to the defect. The added union-of-objects remark describes behaviour identical at the merge-base; it is harmless and does not cancel the recovery. No fix is proposed, so absent.

Quote: "The new `Overwrite` distributes over both union parameters... because the `undefined` member of TType is replaced wholesale by `{b:2}`... A caller can then pass `{b}` alone even though `a` is required". The old Overwrite was distributive over both parameters as well (`TType extends any ? TWith extends any`). At the merge-base, undefined x {b:2} maps to {b:2} too. Scratch tsc probe (clone-work/probe-{base,head}.ts, clone's tsc 5.x, --strict): `const c3: Overwrite<{a:1}|undefined,{b:2}|undefined> = {b:2}` compiles at both base and head. For the realistic `.input(optional obj).use(next)` case, the head no longer accepts `{}` while base did (c6), so it is stricter. The asserted regression is not attributable to the PR.

Quote: "`Overwrite<any,{b:2}>` becomes `{b:2} | {[x:string]:any; ...}`. That is the result for a user context typed `any`... gives middleware and resolvers a union containing a wide index-signature type rather than the overwritten ctx". This names GT-j2's mechanism (`any extends object` takes both branches) and its trigger (context typed any plus a middleware ctx overwrite). The consequence is misdescribed as 'weakens type safety'; the real effect is TS2339 on property access. It still leads a reader to the defect. Fix: "Handle `any` explicitly, for example with `0 extends 1 & T`". The direction is right, but it does not say what the any case should produce (the index-signature merge with the added keys). Partial.

Quote: "It now returns TWith wholesale, where it used to return a merged object... `_ctx_out`... A middleware whose `_ctx_out` is `unknown`, `UnsetMarker` (a symbol) or another primitive would replace the whole accumulated ctx with that value." This is GT-j3's mechanism: the `TType extends object ? (TWith extends object ? merge : TWith)` branch lets a non-object ctx override replace an object context, at the `_ctx_out` call sites. `next<$Context>` is unconstrained (middleware.ts:147). Scratch tsc probe (clone-work/probe-{base,head}.ts, clone's tsc 5.x, --strict): `next({ ctx: u as unknown })` gives TS2339 'base' does not exist on '{}' at head only, and `next({ ctx: maybe|undefined })` gives TS18048 at head only. The item does not name undefined/null specifically, but 'another primitive' covers them. No fix is proposed (Fix: —), so absent.

Quote: "A middleware calls `opts.next({ ctx: maybe })` with `maybe: { extra: number } | undefined`... ctx becomes possibly `undefined` and the resolver fails with TS18048, although `next()` spreads `{ ...callOpts.ctx, ...nextOpts.ctx }`... the merge-base type kept it." This is GT-j3's trigger, mechanism, TS18048 consequence and runtime contradiction exactly. Scratch tsc probe (clone-work/probe-{base,head}.ts, clone's tsc 5.x, --strict) reproduces TS18048 at head only. Fix: a ctx-specific merge at the procedureBuilder and middleware `_ctx_out` sites "that keeps `TType` when `TWith` is `undefined` or `null`", leaving the input fix intact, plus a regression test. That covers every listed manifestation (undefined union, null union, literal undefined) and does not disturb #5020's fix or GT-j1/GT-j2. Sufficient for GT-j3.
